result.result:
I fixed it: text pulled in with `.. include::` now goes through `source-read` before it is parsed. In the issue's example, the included file's `&REPLACE_ME;` now comes out as `REPLACED` in `index.html`. The new test fails on the original code and passes with the fix. Nothing is committed.

**Why it happened:** Sphinx only fired `source-read` when it read each file as a standalone document. That's why the issue's handler did get called for `something-to-include.rst`, but only for that file's own page. When `index.rst` included it, docutils read the file from disk again and parsed it straight away, so the handler's changes never reached `index.html`.

**The fix** is in the `Include` directive in `sphinx/directives/other.py`:
- While the directive runs, Sphinx briefly wraps the docutils method that queues the included lines for parsing (`StateMachine.insert_input`). The included text is sent through `source-read`, and whatever the handlers produce is what gets parsed. The original method is put back afterwards, even if an error occurs.
- The `docname` passed to handlers is the included file's own name if it is a document (e.g. `foo`). Otherwise, such as for a `.txt` file, it is the name of the document doing the including.
- Includes nested inside included files are handled too.
- If nothing is listening to `source-read`, behaviour is exactly as before.

**Tests:**
- I added a test project, `tests/roots/test-directive-include/`, which includes a `.rst` document, `.txt` files, a nested include and an absolute `/text.txt` include from a subfolder.
- Two tests in `tests/test_directive_other.py`:
  - `test_include_source_read_event` checks which docname and text each handler call gets, and that the HTML output has the replaced text.
  - `test_include_without_source_read_listeners` checks that included text is left alone when nobody is listening.

**Docs:** I added a CHANGES entry under "Bugs fixed" and a note with `versionchanged:: 7.2` to the `source-read` event docs in `doc/extdev/appapi.rst`.

**Other test results:** In the related suites (html build, intl, directive_code, environment, duration, intersphinx), 6 tests fail: 2 each in `test_intl.py`, `test_build_html.py` and `test_directive_code.py`. All 6 fail the same way on the original code, so they aren't caused by this change; they look like differences in the installed Pygments version. ruff and mypy aren't installed in the venv, so I didn't run them. I only checked line lengths by hand.

**Side effect:** with `sphinx.ext.duration` on, the time recorded for a document that uses `include` will now be a bit too short. That extension restarts its timer on every `source-read` event, so each include resets it partway through the document.
